back: Three circles (biomass, litter, soil) with areas proportional to nutrient stores, joined by arrows proportional to annual flows.
Large biomass store, small litter and soil stores, fast cycling, high leaching losses.
Medium biomass, moderate litter, larger soil store; slower cycling because of the dry season, fire and grazing.
Photosynthesis, respiration, decomposition, combustion and ocean exchange move carbon between air, living things, soil, oceans and fossil fuels.
Fixation, ammonification, nitrification, assimilation, denitrification and leaching.
Conversion of nitrogen gas into ammonium or nitrates by bacteria (such as Rhizobium in legumes), lightning or industry.
The removal of soluble nutrients from the soil by drainage water.
The biomass store is lost; leaching and erosion remove nutrients; fertility falls within a few years.
Air is about 78% nitrogen and about 21% oxygen; carbon dioxide has risen from about 280 ppm to above 420 ppm.
